source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence: `Let X1, ..., XN be non-negative independent random variables with continuous distributions.`
source_evidence.observation: The exercise fixes a finite family X1, ..., XN and explicitly assumes nonnegativity, independence, and continuous distributions.

source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.2.10 assumption: `Assume that the densities of Xi are uniformly bounded by 1.`
source_evidence.observation: Every Xi has a density, and the family of densities has the common upper bound 1.

source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.2.10(a): `Show that the MGF of Xi satisfies E exp(-tXi) <= 1/t for all t > 0.`
source_evidence.observation: Part (a) asks for the individual estimate E[exp(-t Xi)] <= 1/t for each indexed variable and every positive real t.

binders: A finite index range i = 1, ..., N and real-valued random variables X1, ..., XN (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence).
An arbitrary index i among 1, ..., N (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a), which states the bound for Xi).
A real parameter t satisfying t > 0 (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a), `for all t > 0`).
hypotheses: Each Xi is non-negative (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence).
The random variables X1, ..., XN are independent (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence).
Each Xi has a continuous distribution admitting a density (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence followed by the density assumption).
The densities of the Xi are uniformly bounded above by 1 (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 density assumption).
conclusions: For every i = 1, ..., N and every real t > 0, E[exp(-t Xi)] <= 1/t (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a)).
definitions_and_conventions: The source calls E[exp(-t Xi)] the MGF of Xi at the negative argument -t (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a), `the MGF of Xi satisfies`).
`Densities ... uniformly bounded by 1` supplies one common density upper bound 1 for all Xi (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 density assumption).
Non-negativity restricts the support relevant to the expectation to [0, infinity) (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence).
implicit_context: The expectation and density are taken with respect to the probability law of each Xi (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a), expectation of Xi under the preceding density assumptions).

Part (a) is an individual-variable claim; although independence is inherited from the exercise opening, the displayed estimate itself involves only Xi (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence and part (a)).
Part (b), concerning the small-ball probability for the sum, is not part of the selected claim (PDF page 7; printed page 18, the separate labels `(a)` and `(b)`).

details: The displayed inequality is asserted for each Xi in the family and for every positive real t (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a)).
The conclusion is an expectation bound, not a pointwise bound on the random variable (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a), `E exp(-tXi)`).

Since Xi is non-negative and t > 0, exp(-tXi) is bounded between 0 and 1, so the displayed expectation is finite; this is an analyst inference from the source's non-negativity and positivity assumptions (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening and part (a)).
The numerical constant in the source is exactly 1 both in the common density bound and in the numerator of 1/t (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 assumption and part (a)).

Independence is an explicit inherited assumption of Exercise 2.2.10, even though it is not needed to establish the one-variable inequality in part (a) (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening sentence and part (a)).

undebatable_constraints: The selected result is only Exercise 2.2.10(a), not the sum-probability conclusion in part (b) (PDF page 7; printed page 18, separate part labels).
The variables are non-negative and have continuous distributions with densities uniformly bounded above by the exact constant 1 (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening assumptions).
The bound applies to Xi individually for every positive t and has the exact form E[exp(-t Xi)] <= 1/t (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a)).
The exponential argument is -t Xi, with a minus sign, rather than t Xi (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a)).

ambiguities.issue: The source does not say whether `densities ... uniformly bounded by 1` is intended pointwise for chosen density representatives or essentially almost everywhere.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10: `Assume that the densities of Xi are uniformly bounded by 1.`
ambiguities.impact: The expectation estimate is unchanged under either standard interpretation, because modifying a density on a null set does not change the induced distribution or integral.

ambiguities.issue: The term `MGF` is used for E[exp(-t Xi)] while t is positive, so it is the usual moment-generating function evaluated at the negative parameter -t rather than at t.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10(a): `the MGF of Xi satisfies E exp(-tXi) <= 1/t for all t > 0.`
ambiguities.impact: The displayed formula fixes the intended quantity unambiguously; only the terminology could otherwise invite a sign-convention mismatch.

contract_plain_english: Exercise 2.2.10 fixes non-negative independent random variables X1, ..., XN with continuous distributions whose densities share the upper bound 1. Part (a) claims that for each Xi and every real t > 0, the negative-parameter exponential moment satisfies E[exp(-t Xi)] <= 1/t. Independence is part of the exercise's inherited context but is not needed for this individual-variable estimate. (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Exercise 2.2.10 opening assumptions and part (a).)
